blocks.text: A Content Delivery Network is a globally distributed set of cache servers (points of presence, or PoPs) that sit between users and your origin. When a user requests an image, the nearest PoP serves it from its cache; only on a miss does the PoP fetch from your origin. The payoff is lower latency (the response travels a few milliseconds instead of across an ocean) and massively less load and egress on your origin.

items.label: Latency
items.sub: to a nearby PoP vs 100+ ms cross-ocean

blocks.text: An **origin shield** (a mid-tier cache) means a cold object is fetched from the origin once per region instead of once per PoP, and request collapsing ensures 1,000 simultaneous misses become one origin fetch.

head: Header / technique
Effect
rows: Cache for a year; never revalidate — use with versioned URLs
TTL for shared caches (CDN) separate from browsers
Serve stale content while refreshing in the background
Separate cache entries per header (e.g. Accept-Encoding)

blocks.title: Key insight
blocks.text: Version your static asset URLs (`app.3f9a1c.js`). Then you can cache them forever, and a deploy is just new URLs — no invalidation needed.

cols.title: Versioned URLs
cons: Only for assets you reference by URL you control

cols.title: Purge API
cons: Takes seconds to propagate; rate-limited; easy to forget

cols.title: Short TTLs
cons: More origin traffic; staleness window still exists

items: **Dynamic acceleration:** even uncacheable API requests benefit — the CDN terminates TLS near the user and reuses warm, optimised connections to your origin.
**Edge compute** (Cloudflare Workers, Lambda@Edge): run auth checks, A/B routing, header rewrites or personalisation at the PoP.
**Video:** HLS/DASH segments are small, immutable files — perfect CDN objects.
**Security:** DDoS absorption, WAF rules and bot management live at the edge.

cols.title: Pull (most common)
pros: Caches fill on demand; nothing to upload
cons: First request per PoP is a miss

cols.title: Push
pros: Content is pre-positioned — good for big launches/large files

sections.title: How to use it in an interview

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: All static assets and media go to object storage with versioned keys, fronted by a CDN with long TTLs; the CDN absorbs the egress and our servers only handle API traffic.

items: Say what's cacheable and what's not (personalised responses usually aren't).
Mention cache hit ratio as the metric to watch.
Mention signed URLs/cookies for private content (paid videos).
